components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped and 8 to 15 digits are required after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only create flag. When true, allows registering an owner whose
            lastName and address match an existing owner (i.e. members of the same
            household); otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` household-joining feature for `POST /api/owners`.

**Behavior:** When a create request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, an owner whose `lastName` + `address` match an existing owner is now allowed (instead of being rejected 409), and both the new owner and the matched existing owner(s) are assigned the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on the owner.

**Changes:**

1. **New pipeline step** `AssignOwnerHousehold.java` — runs inside the create transaction after the duplicate check. When `sharesHousehold` is true, it finds existing owners with the same normalized `lastName`+`address` (same normalization rule as `RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold`), derives a stable `HH-<hex>` id from those fields (reusing an existing member's id if one already has it), and assigns it to the new owner and each matched existing owner (persisting the existing ones). No-ops otherwise.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired `assignHousehold` between `rejectHousehold` and `assignCustomerCode`, governed by `transaction` so it commits with the new owner's save.

3. **`Owner` model** — added the `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter.

4. **`openapi.yml`** — added `householdId` as a `readOnly` property on the `Owner` response schema, so it's mapped into `OwnerDto` and returned by both create and GET.

5. **Schemas** — added a `household_id` column to all four `db/*/schema.sql` files, and a trailing `NULL` to the positional owners seed rows in `db/hsqldb/data.sql` (the profile the tests use; h2/mysql/postgres seeds use explicit column lists and needed no change).

The existing `RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold` already short-circuits when `sharesHousehold` is true, so the reject path is unchanged for the opt-out case.
